newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota sees Japanese vehicle sales up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Toyota sees Japanese vehicle sales up in 1997.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp president Hiroshi Okuda expects Japan's domestic vehicle sales in calendar 1997 to rise slightly from the projected 1996 sales of between 5.3 million and 5.4 million units.
He gave his forecast on Tuesday during a gathering of business executives in Nagoya, with Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita in attendance, a Toyota spokesman said.

The Toyota spokesman quoted Okuda as saying that Japan's vehicle sales in 1997 would slightly surpass 1996 levels because of the need for consumers to replace cars bought during the "bubble" era of the late 1980s and strong demand for recreational vehicles.
On Monday, an official at the Japan Automobile Dealers Association said domestic car sales would top 5.30 million units in 1996 and could reach 5.40 million, compared with last year's 5.15 million.
Okuda also said Japan's overall domestic vehicle production would be slightly above 10 million units in 1996.
Japan's vehicle production totalled 10.20 million units in 1995, down 10.4 percent from the previous year.
